chunks: Sahl and Ibn Abi Najran, both together, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
If a man were to dig a well in his house, then a man enters and falls into it, there is nothing upon him, and no responsibility (guarantee), but he should cover it.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal liability of a homeowner if someone falls into their private well?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'la daman' (no liability) for accidental falls in one's private domain, distinguishing between the act of digging and the failure to cover. It emphasizes that while financial compensation is not owed for the accident itself, the owner bears the ethical and legal duty of 'ghitā’' (covering) to prevent recurrence, reflecting the broader legal maxim of preserving property rights while ensuring public safety.

en.hubeali:
Sahl and Ibn Abu Najran, both together from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Musanna Al Hannat, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘If a man were to dig a well in his house, then a man enters and falls into it, there is nothing upon him, and no responsibility, but for covering it’.
